subject: FinBank evals: model recommendations & Redwood setup
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@finbank.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinBank discovery recap + next steps (model recs & evals)

Hi Sara — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key takeaways:
- Primary use case: customer service triage + short-form answer generation for internal ops (document summarization + QC).
- Latency target: P95 < 400ms for single-turn ask during peak; throughput target ~200 qps for async batched jobs.
- Privacy: PII redaction required; FinBank prefers data not leave their VPC for evaluation if possible (we discussed both hosted and private eval runs).
- Success metrics: accuracy on intent classification >= 92% (eval set), average ROUGE-L for summarization >= 0.55, and no quality regressions vs. current baseline LLM.

Our initial model recommendations for evaluation (covering cost/latency/quality tradeoffs):
1) Redwood-compat small: rwd-mini-7b-q4 (fastest, lowest cost) — good baseline for throughput tests
2) Balanced: rwd-medium-13b-8k (better response quality for few-shot prompts)
3) Quality-focused: llama3-70b-q4 (higher-quality generation; evaluate for critical flows)

Links & artifacts I’m attaching/including:
- Eval dataset template (JSONL) — finbank_evals_template.jsonl (attached)
- Redwood benchmark summary (Q1 2026) — https://redwood.ai/docs/benchmarks/2026Q1
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4591

Suggested eval plan:
- You provide a sample labeled dataset (we recommend 500–2,000 examples for first pass). Preferred format: JSONL with fields: id, input, gold. See attached template.
- Dylan (SE) will run the dataset across the three recommended model configs on a shared Redwood eval project. We’ll return: per-example outputs, aggregated metrics (EM, ROUGE, BERTScore), and failure cases.
- Thresholds & regression policy: we’ll set an automated regression alert (50% of runs require manual review if quality drops >3 pts ROUGE-L vs baseline).

Next steps I propose:
1) Send over a sample dataset (500 examples) using the attached template. If VPC-only is required, confirm and we’ll provide onboarding steps for Private evals.
2) Dylan to run initial evals and share results within 48 hours of dataset receipt.
3) Review results together and pick the model (or quantized variant) to pilot in staging.

Let me know if those steps look right or if you want to scope anything else (privacy, encryption, NDA). I’ll follow up with the template and an ask for the technical contact for dataset upload.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: finbank_evals_template.jsonl

From: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@finbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finbank.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: FinBank discovery recap + next steps (model recs & evals)

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the clear plan. A few clarifying points before we send over data:

1) PII/hosting: For the initial eval we can provide a de-identified sample dataset (500 rows). For production we will need a Private deployment; for now we want to confirm if Redwood can run the eval within our VPC (air-gapped) or if you need the sample to be uploaded to Redwood hosted for the first run.
2) Dataset fields: our data team noted some of our examples contain multi-turn context (customer+agent). Is the JSONL template set up for context windows?
3) Timing: if we get the sample over by Thursday (3/5), how quickly can we expect results?

Also looping in Raj (engineering) for technical questions.

—Sara
Sara Thompson
Director, Digital Experience | FinBank
Sara.Thompson@finbank.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@finbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 12:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinBank discovery recap + next steps (model recs & evals)

Hi Sara — happy to jump in. Short answers:

1) VPC/Private evals: Yes — Redwood Private supports running eval jobs inside customer VPCs. For the initial run we can do either: (A) hosted (fastest, <48h turnaround for 500 rows) or (B) Private eval within your VPC (requires a short onboarding: VPN/agent + IAM role; add ~3 business days). Let me know which you prefer.

2) Context / multi-turn: The template supports multi-turn context. Preferred options we accept: 
- JSONL with fields: id, input, gold, metadata.context (if you want structured context) OR
- Flattened prompt: input contains the concatenated prior turns separated by a delimiter (we recommend "\n---\n").

3) Dataset size & timing: For 500 examples we’ll run the three model configs and return detailed results within ~48 hours on hosted. Expect per-model token-cost estimates in the report.

Scoring & export format (high level):
- Exact Match (EM) for structured labels
- ROUGE-L and BERTScore for free-text summaries/answers
- Custom rubric pass/fail for compliance-sensitive outputs (we can add a manual review column)

I’ve pasted a minimal example of the JSONL line we’d like (single-line JSON; we’ll provide the template as an attachment):

{"id": "fb-0001", "input": "Customer: I can’t access my account\nAgent: Have you tried resetting?", "gold": "Reset password flow - send reset link", "metadata": {"context_type": "multi-turn", "priority": "high"}}

If you want, I can run a small smoke test with the first 20 rows as soon as you share them.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.ai

Thanks — that all sounds good. A couple quick notes from engineering:
- We’ll start with a de-identified hosted run for speed. If results look promising we’ll request the Private onboarding.
- Our dataset will include a mix of single-turn and multi-turn samples; we’ll include a context_type metadata flag per-row.
- We expect to send the 500-row sample by EOD Thursday (3/5).

Is there anything special we should include in the metadata for compliance review? For example, ticket id or source system?

Raj Patel
